A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSMGrad research, with matching authors, algorithms, and Cityscapes study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Cityscapes performance results in Table 1, gradient/smoothness observations in Figures 1–2, and runtime measurements in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Cityscapes results in Table 2, gradient/smoothness observations in Figures 1–2, and runtime measurements in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same projected weight updates, regularization, warm-start procedure, stochastic sampling strategy, and Taylor-based fast approximation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Cityscapes seven-class semantic segmentation and depth estimation using SegNet. The revised references to LSTM models concern background examples only.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain STL, MGDA, PCGrad, GradDrop, CAGrad, MoCo, MoDo, Nash-MTL, and SDMGrad. The added related-work table summarizes theoretical guarantees without adding evaluated experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A.3 retain the same model, metrics, SGD training, 200 epochs, batch size 8, hyperparameter search, and test-performance averaging over the last ten epochs.

E4.justification: The gradient-norm/local-smoothness analysis in Figures 1–2 and runtime comparison in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. No ablations, sensitivity analyses, or robustness tests are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report experimental point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All experimental scores match, including Δm% values of 3.93 for GSMGrad and 19.44 for GSMGrad-FA. Reported runtimes remain 2.93 and 1.93 minutes, respectively, and Figures 1–2 use identical plot images.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, convergence guarantees, and proofs in Sections 2–5 and Appendices C–D are unchanged. Equation renumbering and adding a Proof label before the existing Lemma 4 argument introduce no mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both claim the first MOO analysis under generalized smoothness, the same single-loop algorithms and fast approximation, and the same average and iteration-wise CA guarantees. Added comparisons support the retained contribution claims.

C2.justification: The explanations for warm starts, minibatches, fast approximation, and larger iteration-wise costs remain unchanged, as do interpretations of Cityscapes performance and smoothness correlations. No substantive new limitation or applicability boundary is introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains identical implementation details, search ranges, selected hyperparameters, and NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware information. No code or data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: New Table 1 compares existing stochastic methods' smoothness assumptions, boundedness requirements, and sample complexities. Section 1.1 adds explicit iteration-wise complexity comparisons for MoCo, MoDo, and SDMGrad. The cited-work set and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording edits, replaces the RNN background example with LSTM models, distinguishes LSTM and transformer citations, and adds brief comparative discussion. The section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the theoretical comparison table, changes typography and spacing, and reflows the document. The experimental tables become Tables 2–3; their structure and the existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new comparison table and explicit prior-method complexity discussion make the assumptions and contribution easier to assess. More specific neural-network examples and small editorial refinements also improve exposition. These are limited gains in clarity and positioning; the technical results and empirical support remain unchanged.
